title: Model registry entry
description: One row of configs/models.yaml - a candidate (model x precision x backend x platform), NOT a benchmark result. Per docs/note.md §28 the registry is append-only: rows are never deleted, including blocked and deprecated ones, because a negative result (apertus-8b-q4-llamacpp-orin) is part of the experimental record. Self-contained on purpose (no cross-file $ref) so a validator needs no resolver/registry and this repo stays clone-and-run. Conformance levels are documented in schemas/README.md: `required` below is what every row already satisfies today; the fields marked "Phase 3 target" are the docs/note.md §28 additions that become required once configs/models.yaml is backfilled.

model.description: What the serving backend is actually pointed at: a HuggingFace repo id for vLLM (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-AWQ`), or the GGUF repo passed to llama-server's `-hf` for llama.cpp. Not a display name.

revision.description: Phase 3 target. Git revision / commit of the model repo. docs/note.md §3 counts an unpinned revision as an unreproducible experiment: a repo owner can republish weights under the same name.

family.description: Phase 3 target. Qwen2.5 / Bielik / Apertus / ... - the axis a cross-family comparison groups by. Must not be inferred from the `model` string at analysis time.

parameters_b.description: Phase 3 target. Parameter count in billions (1.5, 3, 7, 8, 11). Named `_b` rather than `parameters` because docs/note.md's own example writes `"parameters": 8` meaning billions, which is exactly the kind of unit ambiguity that ruins a merged results table.

architecture.description: Phase 3 target. The checkpoint's own architecture string (`LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, `apertus`). Load-bearing, not cosmetic: llama.cpp rejected Apertus on exactly this field (`unknown model architecture: 'apertus'`), and `llama3_json` was tried for Bielik because it is LlamaForCausalLM-architected.

precision.description: Human-readable precision/quantization summary, written to be read by a person. docs/note.md §23 forbids a bare "INT4": name the actual method. The bielik-11b-awq-vllm-orin row is the standard to match - it records "compressed-tensors int4, group_size=128, symmetric=false" and explicitly flags that this is NOT classic AWQ despite the repo being named `-awq`. Prefer also filling `quantization` below, which is the machine-readable form of the same fact.
examples: compressed-tensors int4, group_size=128, symmetric=false (NOT classic AWQ despite the repo name - see note)

quantization.description: Phase 3 target. Machine-readable form of `precision`, so a quantization study can group by method rather than by string matching. docs/note.md §23: never merge two different methods under one label.

method.description: The actual quantization path, as reported by the checkpoint's own config (vLLM: `quant_method`), not as implied by the repo name.

activation_bits.description: null = activations not quantized (weight-only quantization, the usual case for AWQ/GGUF).

kv_cache_bits.description: KV-cache precision, separate from weights. On a unified-memory board this is often the dominant memory term at long context (docs/note.md §11), so it must not be folded into the weight precision.

calibration_dataset.description: For methods that need calibration (GPTQ, SmoothQuant, some AWQ). null for methods that don't.

quantized_by.description: Who produced the quantized artifact - the model's own authors, or a third party. This repo already distinguishes them for provenance (SpeakLeash's official GGUF vs bartowski's Apertus quant).

backend.description: Serving backend. This enum is deliberately closed and short: docs/note.md §25 says a backend is added only once it actually runs on the target hardware with a reproducible, version-recorded configuration. TensorRT-LLM / TensorRT Edge-LLM are excluded for the reasons in docs/TODO.md Phase 0, not for lack of an enum entry.

backend_image.description: Phase 3 target. The container image this row is served by, when it differs from the coordinator's default. Record a digest where possible: `dustynv/llama_cpp:0.3.9-r36.4.0-cu128-24.04` is a tag, not a llama.cpp version, and this lab has already had to tell builds 4579 / 5058 / 5283 apart by behaviour alone.

platform.description: Which board this row is tuned for. docs/note.md §26: never infer hardware from the config key's name. Serving args are NOT portable across platforms - an Orin row's gpu_memory_utilization is meaningless on a board with different unified memory.

gpu_memory_utilization.description: vLLM only. MUST be set explicitly and conservatively on this hardware: vLLM's own default (0.9) fails outright at startup on a ~30GB unified-memory Orin. See CLAUDE.md's "Memory constraints" for where the current values came from.

max_model_len.description: vLLM only. Every current row is pinned to 2048 for cross-family comparability. Raising it is itself an experimental change (KV cache grows with it) and needs its own memory re-tune - never a silent flag bump. This field was once asserted as "known-good: 4096" without verification and was wrong; `docker inspect` on the real production container settled it at 2048.

quant.description: llama.cpp only. The GGUF quantization file selector passed to `-hf` (`Q4_K_M`). Distinct from `precision`, which is prose, and from `quantization.method`, which is the taxonomy.

n_gpu_layers.description: llama.cpp only. -1 = offload every layer. Unlike the vLLM rows, these values have no prior real measurement to inherit from; re-tune per row if a size doesn't fit.

ctx_size.description: llama.cpp only. The llama-server equivalent of `max_model_len`; keep the two matched across backends or a backend comparison is confounded by context budget.

extra_args.description: Extra CLI args appended to the server command. docs/note.md §40: backend-specific tuning is allowed, but every tuning decision must be documented and reproducible - so anything here needs a sentence in `notes` saying why.

sampling.description: Phase 3 target. Row-specific sampling defaults, when a model documents a required exception (docs/note.md §41 allows exceptions only when documented). Performance benchmarks otherwise pin temperature in the experiment config, not here.

chat_template.description: Phase 3 target. Which chat template was used, if not the tokenizer's own. docs/note.md §21 counts a template change as an experimental change, so it may not live silently inside the benchmark implementation.

tool_call_parser.description: Phase 3 target. vLLM's `--tool-call-parser`. Recorded because it is a real, measured result axis here, not a detail: `hermes` is temperature-robust for Qwen2.5 where llama.cpp's detection is not, and both `hermes` and `llama3_json` fail outright for Bielik on vLLM.

license.description: Phase 3 target. SPDX identifier where one applies. Load-bearing for the parent project: embedded-ai-chain's Phase 5 includes a license audit, and a candidate that can't be shipped is not a candidate.

gated.description: Phase 3 target. Whether the artifact this row actually pulls requires accepting a HuggingFace gate. Both Bielik and Apertus have gated original repos but ungated redistributions, and this lab uses the ungated ones - a staging-reproducibility fact, so it belongs in the registry rather than only in prose.

source.description: Phase 3 target. Provenance of the artifact: the model authors' own repo, or a named third party. This lab already treats the difference as material (SpeakLeash's official GGUF vs bartowski's Apertus quant).

status.description: Phase 3 target, from docs/note.md §28. Machine-readable form of what `notes` already says in prose. `blocked` is a real terminal state with a recorded reason, not a gap to paper over - apertus-8b-q4-llamacpp-orin is blocked because llama.cpp does not recognise its GGUF architecture on any tried build.

notes.description: Required, and required to be honest: configs/models.yaml's own standing rule is that notes must say plainly which claims are CONFIRMED by a real run and which are untested starting points. A row whose numbers are guesses must say so in this field.

then.$comment: llama.cpp-only serving args on a vLLM row are silently ignored by the coordinator, so they would sit in the registry looking authoritative while affecting nothing.
Same in reverse: vLLM-only args on a llama.cpp row are inert and misleading.

examples.notes: CONFIRMED working 2026-09-04: cold start 158-162s, plain and tool-calling completions both succeed. max_model_len=2048 verified against the real production container, not guessed.
